subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & migration considerations (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@luminalabs.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & migration considerations (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — great to learn more about how Lumina Labs uses LLMs for document understanding. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of requirements:
- Production latency target: 200–300ms p95 for 512-token requests
- Data residency / compliance: must keep customer PII in a VPC-managed environment; SOC 2 evidence required
- Traffic profile: steady 200 TPS inference with periodic spikes to ~600 TPS during batch runs
- Migration source: currently on a mix of OpenAI API + an internal GPU cluster for custom models

Options we discussed: 
- Hosted API: fastest to ship, lower ops, but doesn’t meet your VPC requirement for PII workloads
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool (SLA-backed) — good fit for steady throughput and predictable cost; supports KMS integrations and can be network-isolated
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed control plane and on-prem option for full isolation — best for strict compliance or air-gapped needs

Questions to help narrow to a recommendation: 
1) Is the compliance requirement absolute for all PII traffic, or can non-PII calls use Hosted API?
2) Do you anticipate needing on-prem deployment (air-gap) vs VPC-only?
3) Any constraints on migration timing — phased over Q2 or must be done in one go?

Suggested next step: schedule a 30-minute migration workshop with Dev (solutions engineering) to map traffic routing, KV cache reuse, and a migration runbook. I’ll loop him in.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Account Exec — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0191

Attachment: Lumina_Security_Requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@luminalabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@luminalabs.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & migration considerations (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Marissa —

Appreciate the summary. To answer your questions: 
1) Compliance: PII calls must remain inside our VPC-managed environment. Non-PII (analytics / enrichment) can run via hosted if it simplifies rollout, but PII must be isolated.
2) On-prem vs VPC: Not strictly air-gapped today; VPC deployment is preferred. We may request on-prem for specific regulated customers later.
3) Timing: We are aiming for a phased migration in Q2 — prioritize customer-facing endpoints in May, internal batch jobs by June.

Current setup details: 
- Primary: OpenAI API for production routing (fallback to internal cluster for custom models)
- Internal cluster: Nvidia A100 cluster behind a private API; handles heavy batch jobs but has maintenance overhead
- Key ask: We need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs retained for 1 year. Also want to understand cost delta between Dedicated vs Private for our workload profile.

I’ve attached a redacted SOC2 report and our security requirements doc. Please loop in Dev so we can book the workshop.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform — Lumina Labs
alex.johnson@luminalabs.com | +1 (650) 555-0168

Attachment: SOC2_report_redacted.pdf (pdf)
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@luminalabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & migration considerations (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the details and the SOC2 doc — helpful. Quick notes from a technical perspective: 

1) Architecture fit: 
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) will meet your p95 latency and steady throughput goals while giving you predictable cost. We can configure a private subnet and VPC peering so PII traffic stays in your network boundaries.
- Private (VPC) deployment gives you the highest control: customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem agents if you later need air-gap. It’s more ops-heavy and has a higher fixed cost but is recommended if you require strict separation and exclusive tenancy.

2) Migration approach (phased): 
- Phase 1 (May): Route PII production traffic to Redwood Dedicated in a VPC-isolated deployment. Keep OpenAI as fallback for non-PII during the cutover window.
- Phase 2 (June): Migrate batch jobs from internal cluster to Redwood Dedicated or Private depending on approval; we can evaluate quantized model variants to reduce GPU footprint and cost.

3) KMS & audit logs: We support customer KMS integration (Bring Your Own Key) and ship detailed audit logs (token-level request metadata) that can be forwarded to your SIEM. Retention windows can be configured to 1 year.

4) Migration runbook topics for the workshop: routing policies (latency vs cost), model pinning & rollbacks, KV cache warming, and fallback policies. Also want to review your current auth tokens and model artifacts export process.

I’ve proposed a 30-minute workshop link to Marissa; happy to expand to 60 minutes if you want to walk the infra team through the runbook.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

I’ve attached our recommended warm-up plan and a short checklist. We’ll also surface estimated monthly costs in the workshop slides.

Talk soon —
